maya: Quick check — I captured a tiny nsys + torchprof trace for the kv-warmup regression. small tar uploaded (scrubbed) s3://redwood-traces/maya/2311112222-nsys.tgz. Can someone eyeball the flamegraph and kernels? root span shows ~60ms spike.
jon: taking a look :eyes: can you paste the capture commands you used?
maya: Sure, ran:
```
nsys profile -o out --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=cpu --stop-on-exit --capture-range=cudaUser
python -m torch.profiler --start --schedule wait=1,warmup=1,active=3 --activities CPU CUDA --record_shapes --profile_memory --export_chrome_trace=trace.json
```
Also torchprof snippet: `torch.profiler.profile(..., activities=[ProfilerActivity.CPU, ProfilerActivity.CUDA], schedule=torch.profiler.schedule(wait=1, warmup=1, active=3))`
liam: high-level: looks like a lot of memcpys during the kv lookup path. what sequence length and batch are you using?
maya: seq=1024, batch=4. Prefetch enabled (our internal prefetch handler).
sara: try batch=1 and run a 30s micro-capture, or reduce seq to 512 to isolate. also please run with `PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_RECLAIM=1` so the allocator noise is lower.
liam: also check KV cache hit-rate in the trace — flamegraph repeats small kernels which point to thrashing. can you paste the top ops from torchprof (op name + self cpu/cuda time)?
maya: pasted top 10 in a scrubbed gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/maya-kv-top10 (redacted user data). topops show a lot of `aten::copy_` and `cudaMemcpyAsync` dominating cuda time.
perf-bot: automated suggestion: rerun with `--sample-seconds=10 --sample-rate=100` and include `nsys` flag `--output-profile=%t` to keep file sizes down. See profiling docs: https://redwood.internal/eng/runtime/profile-guidelines (internal).
jon: quick glance — torchprof output aligns with memcopy-dominance. likely prefetch buffer causing copies between host<->device. try `--no-prefetch` and set `dataloader num_workers=0` for the micro-capture.
maya: ok re-running with batch=1, no-prefetch, num_workers=0, seq=512 per sara and liam suggestions. I'll also add `--sample-seconds=15`. Posting new tar in ~20m :thumbsup:
liam: thanks — if memcopy still dominates ping me. I can pull per-kernel counters (L2/HBM transfer stats) and run nvprof-like sampling.
maya: follow-up: uploaded new run s3://redwood-traces/maya/2311115822-nsys.tgz. reduced seq to 512 and disabled prefetch. flamegraph looks cleaner, memcpy drops to single-digit ms.
jon: nice quick turnaround. if this removes the regression we can roll a canary with the nvllm-quantized runtime and run the same micro-benchmark under Dedicated to validate.
maya: will open a tiny PR summarizing captures + outcome and link traces. will also add the minimal repro script to the perf artifacts folder. closing the loop later today.
